responsibility: This tutorial example demonstrates the C++ bindings for constructing and executing a trivial numeric libgccjit function. It uses gccjit::context, params, blocks, and operator-style expression helpers to create an exported square function, compile it, look up the resulting symbol, and call it. Compared with the C version, its distinguishing role is showing the same scalar-expression workflow through the inline C++ wrapper API.
same_name_distinction: Unlike gcc/jit/docs/examples/tut02-square.c, this same-stem square example uses the C++ wrapper layer, expressing the same generated function through gccjit objects and wrapper methods rather than raw gcc_jit_* C entrypoints.
